title: Ulyana and the Orchard
premise: Rosalind Voss has built her career on other people's truths, ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrity chef Auguste Lindqvist while hiding a decade of anonymous letters she once exchanged with a stranger during her mother's illness. When the letter-writer — Elias Thorne, an orchardist and former cellist — moves into the cottage beside her late grandmother's house, Rosalind realizes the man she confessed everything to is now the rival memoir's key source, and exposing her double life could end her. As the orchard's inheritance dispute forces them together, Rosalind must choose between protecting the career that paid her mother's debts and the love that was ten years in the making; she confesses everything in the final chapter, losing the Lindqvist contract but gaining the orchard, Elias, and a found family among the village keepers of her grandmother's trees.
about_author: Gideon Thackeray is the pen name of a former orchard worker turned novelist who spent six seasons grafting apples in the Kentish Weald before writing full-time. Known for quiet, sensory romances about people who mistake discipline for safety, Thackeray lives beside a working orchard tended by a cooperative of neighbors.

chapters.title: The Muscle of the Heart
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In a London hotel bar, she watches Auguste Lindqvist charm a publisher with words she wrote, rehearsing her belief that the heart is trainable and containable. She signs the contract for his memoir. Emotional beat: control asserted, cracks hidden.

chapters.title: Provisions of the Estate
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A solicitor's letter reveals her grandmother left her half of Hollowmere Orchard — with the condition she live there one full year. She resents the timing, mid-memoir. Beat: duty arrives disguised as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Cottage Next Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Arriving at the village, she finds a moving van at the neighboring cottage and a man unloading a cello. Their first exchange is prickly over a fallen fence. Beat: irritation masking recognition she can't name.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Flashback, Rosalind's POV. Ten years earlier, during her mother's illness, she wrote to a pen-pal service and poured out everything to 'E.' The letters ended when he stopped replying. Beat: the wound that made her a ghostwriter.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He explains to skeptical villagers why he bought the cottage: he grew up here, and the orchard was the only place his music ever made sense. He recognizes Rosalind's surname from old letters. Beat: hope, carefully rationed.

chapters.title: Windfall Apples
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A storm scatters fruit across both properties; she and Elias spend a day gathering it, and the conversation turns startlingly easy. She almost mentions the letters, then doesn't. Beat: intimacy outpacing caution.

chapters.title: The Memoir's Missing Chapter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, in a call with her editor. Auguste's memoir needs a redemption arc, and his people mention a 'cellist friend from the countryside' as a source. Rosalind goes cold. Beat: two worlds beginning to collide.

chapters.title: Cider at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Village POV, mainly the Coopers, the orchard's tenant family. They welcome Elias to the pressing day and size up Rosalind as 'the Voss girl who never came back.' Beat: the village as chorus and judge.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He shows Rosalind the tree her grandmother grafted the year Rosalind was born. She is moved despite herself, and he nearly tells her about the letters. Beat: tenderness with a held breath.

chapters.title: Interview Request
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Auguste's assistant emails: they've located Elias Thorne and want him interviewed for the memoir. Rosalind realizes she may have to ghostwrite the story of the man she loves. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Year's First Frost
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She and Elias cover the young trees together through the night; by dawn she has told him things she's told no one — except, once, a stranger on paper. Beat: the past pressing against the present.

chapters.title: E.
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He confirms it: Rosalind is his letter-writer, the girl who stopped writing when his family scandal broke and he was too ashamed to explain. He decides to tell her — then overhears a phone call hinting at her secret work. Beat: recognition and retreat.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She interviews Elias for the memoir under a pretext, hating every transcription, while his answers are quietly addressed to the girl he thinks betrayed him. Beat: two people lying by omission in the same room.

chapters.title: The Cooper Children
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The tenant Coopers face eviction by the orchard's other half-owner; their eldest, Marnie, apprentices herself to Rosalind and Elias. Beat: found family begins assembling around the trees.

chapters.title: A Decade of Silence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He finally shows Rosalind a shoebox: her own letters, kept ten years. She realizes he is E. — and that he believes she abandoned him after his father's fraud conviction. Beat: the central revelation, and the first rupture.

chapters.title: Trainable, Containable
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tries to explain the letters stopped because her mother died that same month; grief, not judgment. He wants to believe her. They do not resolve it. Beat: love against the habit of self-protection.

chapters.title: Auguste Descends
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV. The celebrity chef arrives in the village for color and authenticity, delighted by the orchard, oblivious to the havoc his memoir is causing. Beat: the rival made human and more dangerous for it.

chapters.title: Ghostwritten
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Auguste, charmed by Elias, asks Rosalind to draft the 'orchard redemption' chapter from her own observations. She writes Elias's soul into someone else's book. Beat: self-betrayal made concrete.

chapters.title: Marnie's Map
chapters.summary: Marnie's POV. The girl discovers the deed dispute hinges on a boundary her grandfather recorded in a hand-drawn map hidden in the pressing house. Beat: the inheritance plot turns; hope for the Coopers.

chapters.title: The Press House Argument
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Elias, alternating. A blazing fight: he accuses her of still hiding behind other people's words; she accuses him of loving an idea of her from ten years ago. Beat: midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: Winter Pruning
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, he prunes the trees badly and admits the fault was his — he let shame answer her silence with silence. Marnie, blunt as a pruning saw, tells him so. Beat: humility begins.

chapters.title: The Draft Leaks
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A chapter of the memoir draft circulates in the village; Elias's private history is in it, in words Rosalind wrote. He assumes she sold him out. Beat: the lowest point between them.

chapters.title: What the Contract Says
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reads her own contract and finds a morality-and-consent clause she could invoke — at the cost of the career that paid her mother's debts. Beat: the choice sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: Snow on the Grafts
chapters.summary: Village POV. The community quietly shelters the trees and the Coopers through a hard cold snap; Rosalind, working among them, is claimed by the village without her asking. Beat: found family solidifies.

chapters.title: Confession, Draft One
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She writes Elias a letter — her first in ten years — explaining everything: the ghostwriting, the fear, the mother's death. She doesn't send it. Beat: truth rehearsed but not risked.

chapters.title: Auguste's Offer
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV. Genuinely fond of Rosalind, he offers to make her co-author, publicly credited — if the orchard chapter stays as written. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: The Boundary Walk
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Elias, alternating. Forced to survey the disputed boundary together for the deed case, they walk the orchard's edge and, exhausted, finally speak honestly about the letters. Beat: thaw.

chapters.title: Marnie's Discovery
chapters.summary: Marnie's POV. The old map proves the Cooper tenancy and half the orchard belong under one deed — Rosalind's. She holds the Coopers' home in her hands. Beat: power arrives with weight.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the land registry hearing she presents the map, saving the Coopers, and publicly aligns herself with the village against the memoir's version of events. Beat: duty and love begin pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Auguste's publisher threatens litigation over the boundary testimony; her editor gives her a day to recant or be dropped. Beat: the career that saved everything now demands her silence.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter, Read
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Marnie, playing courier and matchmaker, delivers Rosalind's unsent letter. Elias reads a decade of her truth in one sitting and walks through the snow to her door. Beat: grace offered before it's earned.

chapters.title: Spring Sap
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Elias, alternating. They reconcile properly — not with a grand gesture but with a plan: he'll play again, she'll write under her own name. Beat: love chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: The Chapter She Won't Write
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tells Auguste she will not draft the orchard chapter as fiction; he may tell the truth or lose her. He asks for a day. Beat: the stand taken.

chapters.title: Publication Eve
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV. Torn between his manufactured redemption arc and the real one he witnessed, Auguste reads Rosalind's resignation letter and the village's petition side by side. Beat: the antagonist's conscience.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Village POV. At the blossom festival, Auguste publicly reads the true chapter — crediting 'R. Voss, who taught me that a ghost deserves a name' — and withdraws the false material. Beat: public vindication, at a price.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The publisher drops her; her agent calls it professional suicide; Rosalind feels lighter than she has in a decade. She signs the papers making the orchard a cooperative with the Coopers. Beat: loss reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: First Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A small press accepts her proposal for a book about orchards, grief, and letters — to be published as Rosalind Voss. Elias reads the first page over her shoulder. Beat: the ghostwriter incarnate.

chapters.title: Blossom
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He plays the cello under the flowering trees while the village — Coopers, keepers, Auguste unexpectedly among them — gathers for the year's first pressing. Beat: found family in full bloom.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She mails one final letter to E., addressed to the cottage next door, telling him everything the girl of ten years ago couldn't. He reads it standing in her doorway. Beat: the circle closed.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She learns her grandmother's secret: Ulyana was the pen-pal service volunteer who first paired two lonely strangers a decade ago — a final gift from beyond. Rosalind plants a new graft with Elias and Marnie. Beat: love, duty, and inheritance reconciled in a single tree.
